title: 6Sense Filter
subtitle: Six-dimensional qualification screening that turns the costly question "should we invest?" into a structured, evidence-based answer — before equity is committed.

sections.heading: The 6-Dimensional Architecture
sections.body:
The 6Sense Filter™ evaluates ventures across six operational pillars. A startup must pass all six — the filter exists to say no early and cheaply:

\- Direction — Is the problem real, the market sizeable, and the founder thesis credible?

\- Energy — Is the business model sustainable? (CLV:CAC ≥ 3:1 is the minimum threshold.)

\- Capacity — Does the team and infrastructure have the OEE and CCC metrics to execute?

\- Prioritisation — Is the roadmap sequenced for capital efficiency, not feature maximalism?

\- Risk — Does the EMV model account for regulatory exposure, not just commercial risk?

\- Decision — Does the leadership team have the governance capability to make hard calls under pressure?

Decision holds absolute veto power. A company that cannot make structured decisions under uncertainty will fail regardless of the other five dimensions.

sections.heading: Turning Regulatory Complexity into Moat
sections.body:
Traditional venture qualification frameworks fail in high-barrier industries because they treat compliance as cost. 6Sense embeds regulatory architecture, cybersecurity posture, and data governance directly into early-stage evaluation.

A company that clears the 6Sense filter in a regulated domain has already begun building the barriers that keep competitors out. Regulation is not a burden — it is the moat, if you structure for it early.

sections.heading: Information Asymmetry as the Core Problem
sections.body:
Early-stage markets are lemons markets. Founders make claims; investors cannot easily verify them. The 6Sense process is, economically, an information-asymmetry reduction machine — each dimension converts founder claims into verifiable evidence before equity is committed.

The filter also embeds adoption realism: addressable market claims are discounted by diffusion position. A product that requires laggard-segment adoption to hit plan fails the Direction dimension regardless of headline TAM.
